concerns.text: User Story US-3 states the evaluation will use a *paired t‑test* for statistical significance, but FR-005 (and SC-004) require a *McNemar’s test*. The two tests are mutually exclusive, creating a direct contradiction in the statistical methodology.

FR-005 mandates the use of McNemar’s test on binary success outcomes, yet the earlier US-3 description and the power‑analysis FR-007 assume a paired‑t‑test framework. This inconsistency makes the statistical plan internally incoherent.

FR-007 specifies an a‑priori power analysis using Cohen’s d (effect size for a paired‑t‑test) while the actual test (per FR-005) is McNemar’s test. Power calculations for McNemar differ, so the claimed ≥ 0.8 power for N = 500 is unsupported.
US-5 includes a self‑reference “(See US‑5)”, which is a circular citation and adds no value; it should reference a different artifact or be removed.
